title: ICE Detainee Lianyong Wei Dies Hours After Intake at Saipan Facility; 57th Death Since Trump's Second Term Began
excerpt: Lianyong Wei, a 51-year-old Chinese national, was found unresponsive the morning after being taken into ICE custody at a facility in Saipan, Northern Mariana Islands, marking the 57th detainee death since January 2025 and the 24th of 2026.
content:
Lianyong Wei, 51, a Chinese national whose immigration status had lapsed, was arrested by Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands authorities on August 21, 2026, and transferred to ICE custody the following day. He was found unresponsive during morning checks at the Saipan facility on August 23 and was pronounced dead at approximately 7:30 a.m. local time after emergency interventions at the Commonwealth Health Care Corporation Emergency Room.

  • Wei's death was the 57th death of an immigrant detainee in federal custody since the start of President Trump's second term, according to ICE's detainee death notifications.
  • Twenty-four of those 57 deaths had occurred since January 1, 2026.
  • ICE's June 2026 policy change — eliminating the requirement to report deaths occurring within 30 days after release — meant that the official count excluded several additional deaths, including one at Delaney Hall in which a man died at a hospital after being released during a seizure.

NPR and Georgia Public Broadcasting reported on the broader pattern, noting that Wei's death came as the 2026 death toll was on pace to break the 2025 record. Advocacy groups pointed to systemic failures in medical screening and care as underlying causes.
